_comment: Commands the e2e scenarios send, by scenario name and platform family (unix = Linux and macOS). Each value is the exact form the Rewst trigger expects (JSON-quoted); send-command, assert-log-contains and the it-scripts resolve a scenario name here so the workflow and matrix carry no per-platform command text (sc-126318).

success.windows:
"[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

$PS_Results = New-Object -TypeName psobject

# Start of typed powershell
$PS_Results | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name \"error\" -Value \"\"
$PS_Results | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name \"output\" -Value \"hello world`n\"

# Post results back to Rewst
$postData = $PS_Results | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Method \"Post\" -Uri $post_url -Body $postData -ContentType \"application/json\""

patterns.unix:
Command completed
Sending postback
Postback sent
patterns.windows:
Command completed
Sending postback
Postback already sent

success._note: The Windows form is the engine's typed-PowerShell self-posting script, which is why its log pattern ends in 'Postback already sent' where unix ends in 'Postback sent'.

failure.windows:
"[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

$PS_Results = New-Object -TypeName psobject

# Start of typed powershell
throw \"this is a test error\"

# Post results back to Rewst
$postData = $PS_Results | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Method \"Post\" -Uri $post_url -Body $postData -ContentType \"application/json\""

sweep._note: Long enough to outlive the engine's ~165 s ceiling: the sweep scenario force-kills the agent while this is still running.

verbose._note: 200 MiB to stdout, then a clean exit. Quote-free and backslash-free so it survives the trip through the trigger's JSON-quoted commands field unchanged, and byte-exact so the produced counts the agent reports are predictable; three orders of magnitude past the ceiling the scenario configures, so the RSS ceiling asserted while it runs is far below what buffering the output whole would cost (sc-106105).

verbose_stderr._note: A short stdout line, then 200 MiB to stderr (sc-106105; see verbose).

verbose_hang._note: 200 MiB to stdout, then a hang past the command timeout (sc-106105; see verbose).

child_process_hang._note: Windows-only descendant-tree kill scenario (sc-108853): spawns a detached child via Start-Process tagged with a distinctive sleep duration (91743 s) used purely as a process-list marker, then hangs the parent past the configured command timeout. Single quotes stand in for the nested double quotes Start-Process's -ArgumentList would otherwise need, keeping the payload double-quote- and backslash-free like the verbose scripts.

quick._note: A command that finishes at once and does not post its own result (unlike the Windows `success` form), so the engine sees exactly the agent's postback - the sc-126322 spool, lost-PUBACK and journal-full scenarios count those.

hold._note: Occupies the single worker long enough for the journal-full scenario (sc-126322) to queue more commands than the integration build's 20-entry journal holds; the scenario installs with --command-timeout-seconds 120 so the integration build's 5 s default timeout does not cut it short.
